clue.text: Notes made by one in my journal at the front

indicators.note: at the front says the journal piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: a journal is a newspaper, a paper

indicators.note: in says the word one sits inside the word my

parts.note: taken as written, M and Y
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone jotting notes in their diary, with the journal at the front of the notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like jottings in the journal, but means banknotes; 'in' places one inside my, and 'at the front' puts the journal word first.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are currency printed on paper rather than coins.

clue.text: Overtake father with two sons

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
S is the abbreviation for son, used twice

explanation.surface: A father driving with his two boys pulls out past another car.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass another vehicle on the road is to overtake it.

clue.text: Cardinal rule, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word heard the same as the word for rule, spelt differently

parts.note: a principle is a rule or law

explanation.surface: Reads like a church rule, perhaps one laid down by a cardinal, passed on by hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' looks like the churchman, but here it is the adjective meaning chief, as in cardinal sins or cardinal points.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means main or most important, the same as principal.

clue.text: Swift attack seizing power

indicators.note: seizing says the attack word grabs and holds the power letter inside it

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A quick military strike to grab control of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid and swift are synonyms, both meaning very fast.

clue.text: Where one may find fruit or variety of beet

parts.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy vegetable that is a variety of beet

explanation.surface: A gardener's choice: grow fruit, or plant some chard instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, so it is a place you would expect to pick apples or plums.

clue.text: Outside, passing by non-stop

indicators.note: passing here means going away, so the by letter drops out of the outside word

parts.note: external means outside
X is the multiplication sign, read as by (three by four)

explanation.surface: Someone going past the outside of a building without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is X as in measurements like 3 x 4; take X out of EXTERNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eternal goes on for ever, without any end or break.

clue.text: Ringing some of the choristers

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a choir singing loudly in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing sound reverberates; an echo is a sound that rings back off walls.

clue.text: Member of the clergy soon after beginning of chaplaincy

indicators.note: after says the soon word follows the letter from chaplaincy
beginning of says only the opening letter of chaplaincy is used

parts.note: first letter of chaplaincy
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A clergyman joins the staff shortly after a chaplaincy starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a priest attached to a cathedral, one of the clergy.

clue.text: Magical words of Aesop seem silly about lion's tail

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the letter from the lion
silly says the letters of Aesop seem are jumbled foolishly

parts.note: the letters of these two words are rearranged

indicators.note: tail says only the final letter of lion is used

parts.note: last letter of lion

explanation.surface: A fable by Aesop, with its lion, seems a silly source for a magic spell.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged AESOPSEEM wraps round N, the end of 'lion'. The phrase opens the robbers' cave in Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the spell that opens the cave in the Arabian Nights tale, a phrase of magic.

clue.text: Page carries on, takes liberties

parts.note: resumes means carries on after a pause

explanation.surface: A cheeky pageboy keeps going, overstepping the mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To presume is to act overboldly, assuming a right one does not have.

clue.text: Getting married in spring? Tighten one's belt

indicators.note: in says the married letter goes inside the spring word

parts.note: to skip is to spring lightly

explanation.surface: A spring wedding means the couple must economise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is the verb to leap, SKIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightening one's belt is an idiom for spending less, as does someone who skimps.

clue.text: Sanction demolition

explanation.surface: Planners approve knocking down a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both authorisation to proceed and the removal of old buildings from a site.

clue.text: Form of pollution — a constant one with sewer

parts.note: C is the physics symbol for a constant, the speed of light
I is the Roman numeral for one
a drain is a sewer

explanation.surface: A sewer leaking all the time is a source of pollution.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain made acidic by sulphur and nitrogen emissions is a well-known environmental pollutant.

clue.text: Beaches in outskirts of Skegness?

indicators.note: outskirts are the outer edges, so the outer letters of Skegness are meant: one S and another S

parts.note: the first and last letters of Skegness are an S and an S

explanation.surface: A question about where to find beaches around Skegness, a seaside resort on the English east coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of Skegness are S and S; run together as one word that is the answer, and the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Sands are stretches of sandy shore, the plural noun for seaside beaches.

clue.text: Editorials with it must give guidance

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper editorial, the leading article
it means fashionable, as does hip

explanation.surface: Newspaper editorials that are with it should steer opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is the act of directing others, giving them direction.

clue.text: Former partner modelled naked

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
posed, as an artist's model does

explanation.surface: An ex sat nude for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposed means uncovered and bare, so open to view like a nude body.

clue.text: Famous duo, male, sounding frank when broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer whose voice comes across as candid on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio but here means scattered. Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel were the American folk-rock pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The American singing pair of Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel are one of pop music's best-known double acts.

clue.text: Tells stories about cat in French city

indicators.note: about says the stories word goes around the cat word

parts.note: to tell stories is to lie, so lies
mog is British slang for a cat

explanation.surface: Someone spins tales about a cat living in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Limoges is a city in west-central France, famous for its porcelain.

clue.text: See 16
Quandary of Miss Woodhouse after I'd returned then left

indicators.note: after says Emma comes behind the other pieces
returned says I'd is turned round

parts.note: taken as I and D
Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's Emma

explanation.surface: Puzzling over Austen's Emma once one has come back and gone away again.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma Woodhouse is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel Emma; 'after' puts her name last, behind the turned-round I'd and the left letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a difficult choice between options, which is a quandary.

clue.text: London theatre's adaptation of Lady C enthralling wife and husband

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the London theatre is the answer

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the rearranged letters hold the wife letter inside
an adaptation reworks the original, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Lady and C are rearranged

explanation.surface: A West End theatre staging a version of Lady Chatterley's Lover with a married couple.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady C is Lady Chatterley. 'adaptation of' turns LADYC into ALDYC, 'enthralling' puts W inside to give ALDWYC, then H is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aldwych is a West End playhouse on the Strand-side street of the same name in London.

clue.text: Odd sort, odd making stand

indicators.note: odd means irregular, so the letters are put in an irregular order

parts.note: the letters of sort are rearranged
rum is a British word for odd or strange

explanation.surface: A strange sort of person, an oddity, taking a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised platform for a speaker, a kind of stand or podium.

clue.text: Change the appearance of rocker's rival in part of film

indicators.note: in says the rival goes inside the film word

parts.note: a reel is a section of film
mods and rockers were rival British youth gangs of the 1960s

explanation.surface: A 1960s film where a rocker's rival gets a makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods (scooters, sharp suits) and rockers (motorbikes, leather) were feuding 1960s British youth subcultures.
explanation.definitionFit: To remodel something is to alter its shape or look, giving it a new form.

clue.text: Bird, yellow, heading off

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter of the yellow word is removed

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, as does craven

explanation.surface: A yellow bird flying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow' looks like a colour but means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Minister starts to visit Irish churches at random

indicators.note: starts says the first letter of each following word is used

parts.note: first letter of visit
first letter of Irish
first letter of churches
first letter of at
first letter of random

explanation.surface: A clergyman drops in on Irish churches unpredictably.
explanation.definitionFit: A vicar is a parish priest, a minister of the Church of England.

clue.text: Work on mock trial

indicators.note: on says the work word follows the mock word

parts.note: dummy means mock or imitation
to run a machine is to work it

explanation.surface: A lawyer preparing a mock trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy run is a rehearsal or practice attempt, a test before the real thing.

clue.text: Poet certainly receiving a bouquet at the end

indicators.note: receiving says the yes word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: yes, certainly, as a reply

indicators.note: at the end says only the final letter of bouquet is used

parts.note: last letter of bouquet

explanation.surface: A poet happily accepting flowers after a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish poet and Nobel laureate.

clue.text: Ever so clever youth, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A young person who is ever so bright, partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is an informal intensifier meaning extremely, the same as very.

clue.text: Overworked in area of East London by editor

indicators.note: by says the editor letters sit beside the area

parts.note: Hackney is a borough of East London

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor in Hackney, worked off their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overworked' looks like a tired person but describes an over-used phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackneyed phrase is stale from overuse, used too often to have any force.

clue.text: Rejecting starter, cause annoyance in joint

indicators.note: rejecting the starter means the first letter is thrown out

parts.note: to rankle is to cause lasting annoyance

explanation.surface: A diner sends back the first course, irritating someone in a joint, a cheap restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a cheap eatery, and 'starter' a first course; here joint is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge connecting foot and leg, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: Leave — usual time

parts.note: par means the usual or normal level, as in par for the course

explanation.surface: An employee's leave at the normal time.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to go away from someone, to depart.

clue.text: Something easily done in Peter Pan, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a task that is very easy
second meaning: a play for children, as J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan is

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer literally for the second sense: a stage play written for a child audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes any task so simple that a youngster could do it.
